episodes.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. Now what?
episodes.about: Security expert Alex Stamos tells Nilay Patel that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we have known it is all but doomed, thanks to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks. That disruption opens a lot of places where bad actors can get in while everyone else scrambles. Stamos is not a doomer in the long run, but he does think there is a dark age to get through before things get better.
episodes.why: Out today: Stamos, as direct as he gets, on why AI-boosted attacks broke the old security industry, and the dark age he says comes before AI-versus-AI defense catches up.

episodes.title: Why AI Goes Rogue: Turing Award Winner Explains Reward Failure | Andrew Barto
episodes.about: Andrew Barto helped found reinforcement learning. He and Richard Sutton wrote the field's standard textbook, and they shared the Turing Award for that work. Reinforcement learning now trains today's reasoning models and AI agents. It also sits behind some of their strangest behavior, including the recent cases of agents breaking out of their sandboxes. Craig Smith visited Barto at his home on Cape Cod to talk about where rewards come from and why they are so hard to get right - including Barto's admission that boiling every goal down to a single number is a weakness in his own framework.
episodes.why: The co-inventor of reinforcement learning on reward failure - the mechanism behind agents escaping their sandboxes - tracing the problem back to Norbert Wiener's warnings in the 1950s.

episodes.title: Controlling Biology - Fabian Theis, Helmholtz Munich
episodes.about: Fabian Theis of Helmholtz Munich has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept - the push to build AI models of cells - and his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand biology at multiple scales and across multiple kinds of data at once. The conversation covers where virtual-cell models actually stand and what it would take for them to move from describing biology toward predicting and controlling it.
episodes.why: Virtual cells from the lab pushing the algorithms furthest: what multi-scale, multi-modal models can now say about how a cell will behave, and what is still missing.

episodes.title: Companies Are Spending 5x More on AI Now
episodes.about: Companies are spending nearly five times more on AI than last year, and agents are driving the surge. NLW breaks down Menlo Ventures' latest enterprise AI report, exploring why spending is blowing past budgets, how Anthropic and OpenAI are capturing the market, and what the shift from seats to tokens means for businesses. In the headlines: a massive market selloff, uncertainty around Anthropic's IPO, and METR's report on AI accelerating AI research.
episodes.why: Out today, built on Menlo's new enterprise report: spending up nearly 5x in a year with agents driving it, and the seat-to-token shift underneath the headline number.

episodes.title: Ep 97: Jev Creator on Decision Models, Benchmark Fatigue & Why the Labs Missed It
episodes.about: Diogo Almeida coauthored OpenAI's InstructGPT paper and spent two years in stealth building Jev, a 'system one' model from TypeSafe AI that returns structured decisions instead of text, which launched in September. He and Jacob Effron discuss why AI still isn't automating the easy work it has been smart enough to do for years, why almost every LLM call should be meant for a machine, benchmark fatigue and copycat releases, and his estimate that coding agents deliver a 20 to 40% speedup.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Unsupervised Learning is Redpoint's interview show, new here: an InstructGPT coauthor explains why he left text behind and built a model that returns decisions instead of words.
